method: Single-gene physical traits from Dog10K-imputed genotypes (GP >= 0.8) with read-level calls for indels, insertions and copy-number events (canFam4 coordinates from OMIA and flank-mapped literature positions; see analysis/traits/).

traits.name: Coat length
traits.description: Long coats need two long-hair (Lh) copies in total across the FGF5 variants (recessive). Lh1 is the common one; Lh2-Lh5 are breed-specific.

traits.name: Furnishings
traits.description: A 167-letter insertion near RSPO2 gives the mustache, beard and eyebrows of Schnauzers, terriers and doodles. One copy is enough (dominant); furnished dogs shed little whatever their shedding gene says.

traits.name: Coat curl
traits.description: KRT71 curl variants make long coats wavy (one copy) or curly (two copies); furnishings add curl of their own.

traits.name: Shedding
traits.description: The MC5R variant (Thr237) lowers shedding; dogs with two copies shed lightly, others heavily or seasonally. Furnished dogs are light shedders regardless.

traits.name: Hairlessness (Xolo type)
traits.description: A 7-letter duplication in FOXI3 causes the hairlessness of Xoloitzcuintli, Chinese Crested and Peruvian Inca Orchid; one copy is hairless, two copies do not survive.

traits.name: Hairlessness (terrier type)
traits.description: The SGK3 deletion of the American Hairless Terrier; hairless only with two copies.

traits.name: Albinism (Doberman type)
traits.description: A 4,081-letter deletion in SLC45A2; two copies cause oculocutaneous albinism (white coat, pink skin, light eyes).

traits.name: Saddle tan
traits.description: A 16-letter duplication near RALY is a marker for the tan-point pattern: two copies favour black-and-tan; the pattern only shows in tan-pointed dogs. A marker, not the cause.

traits.name: Red pigment intensity
traits.description: Five positions explain most of the difference between deep red and cream in yellow/red fur (Slavney 2021). Counting the intensifying alleles gives the shade.

traits.name: Muzzle length
traits.description: The BMP3 F452L variant is the best-known muzzle-length gene: two copies give a short muzzle (Bulldog, Pug), one or none a medium or long one. At least five genes shape the snout.

traits.name: Tail length
traits.description: One copy of the T-gene variant gives a natural bobtail (Corgi, Australian Shepherd, Brittany); two copies do not survive.

traits.name: Hind dewclaws
traits.description: Regulatory variants near LMBR1 (the limb enhancer of SHH) give roughly a 50% chance of hind dewclaws per carrier; other genes contribute.

traits.name: Back muscling and bulk
traits.description: An X-linked ACSL4 variant adds heavy back muscling and about 12 kg in bulky large breeds (Rottweiler, Bernese, St Bernard). Males need one copy, females two.

traits.name: Blue eyes (non-merle)
traits.description: A 98-kb duplication upstream of ALX4 is behind most blue eyes in Huskies and tri-colour Australian Shepherds; one copy raises the chance of blue eyes.

traits.name: Body size 1
traits.description: The IGF1 small-dog haplotype (tagged by an intron SNP in complete linkage with the SINE insertion) is the single biggest size gene: each copy takes off several kilograms.

traits.name: Body size 2
traits.description: The IGF1R R204H variant reduces adult size; each copy takes off several kilograms.

traits.name: Body size 4
traits.description: The GHR E191K growth-hormone-receptor variant reduces adult size.

traits.name: Body size 5
traits.description: The GHR P177L variant is one of the strongest small-size alleles (about 10 kg per copy).

traits.name: Altitude adaptation
traits.description: The EPAS1 G305S variant, shared with Tibetan Mastiffs and high-altitude wolves, improves tolerance of low oxygen.

traits.name: Appetite
traits.description: A 14-letter deletion in POMC (common in Labradors and Flat-coated Retrievers) removes two satiety signals: carriers are more food-motivated and prone to weight gain.
